# Coherent same-lattice multi-window collapse

**Status:** `PROPOSED NATIVE THEOREM / EXACT FULL-LATTICE FRAME ALGEBRA`

This theorem closes a substantially larger class than block-direct sums. Any finite family of windows placed on the same complete critical modulation lattice is exactly equivalent, up to coefficient-space zero directions, to one scalar window whose squared modulus is the aggregate channel power.

The conclusion holds for the entire compressed Hermitian form, not only for its first two traces.

## 1. Full-lattice setup

Let `I` be an interval of length `L`, and let

```text
e_k(u)=L^(-1/2) exp(-2 pi i k u/L),  k in Z,
```

be the Fourier basis of `H=L2(I)` after translating `I` to the origin.

Fix finitely many bounded windows

```text
phi_1,...,phi_q in L-infinity(I)
```

and put

```text
psi(u)=[sum_(a=1)^q |phi_a(u)|^2]^(1/2).
```

Assume `psi>0` almost everywhere on its effective support. Multiplying a channel by a fixed modulation merely changes `phi_a`, so fixed channel offsets are included.

Let `F:ell2(Z)->H` be Fourier synthesis,

```text
F c=sum_k c_k e_k.
```

Define the scalar and multi-window synthesis maps

```text
S_psi d       = psi Fd,
S_phi(c_1,...,c_q)=sum_a phi_a F c_a.
```

## 2. Exact coisometry

Define, in the time domain,

```text
R(g_1,...,g_q)
  =sum_a [phi_a/psi] g_a,
```

with the ratio set to zero on the null set where `psi=0`. Then

```text
R R*=I
```

on the effective scalar space, because pointwise

```text
sum_a |phi_a/psi|^2=1.
```

Transporting through Fourier synthesis gives the coefficient-space coisometry

```text
U=F* R (direct_sum_a F),
U U*=I.
```

The synthesis maps satisfy exactly

```text
boxed: S_phi=S_psi U.                                  (MW1)
```

## 3. Compression equivalence theorem

Let `B` be any Hermitian sesquilinear form on the common physical range for which the following coefficient matrices are defined:

```text
G_psi=S_psi* B S_psi,
G_phi=S_phi* B S_phi.
```

Then

```text
boxed: G_phi=U* G_psi U.                              (MW2)
```

Since `U` is a coisometry, after unitary identifications of coefficient spaces it has the normal form

```text
U=[I  0].
```

Consequently

```text
boxed: G_phi is unitarily equivalent to G_psi direct_sum 0.  (MW3)
```

In particular the two compressions have exactly the same:

- nonzero eigenvalues with multiplicity;
- positive and negative indices;
- rank;
- trace and every trace power for which they are defined;
- Schatten norms;
- rank–trace and threshold-count certificates.

### Proof

Equation `(MW1)` is the pointwise identity

```text
psi sum_a (phi_a/psi)F c_a=sum_a phi_a F c_a.
```

Equation `(MW2)` follows by substitution. Every coisometry is unitarily equivalent to the projection from a larger Hilbert space onto the target, which gives `(MW3)`. `square`

## 4. Poisson-kernel form

The same collapse is visible directly in the Gabor kernel. With the paper's Fourier convention and critical spacing `h=2pi/L`, let

```text
f_(a,k)(u)=phi_a(u) exp(-i tau_k u),
tau_k=T+kh.
```

For real frequencies `tau,tau'`, Poisson summation gives

```text
sum_(a,k in Z)
  hat(phi_a)(tau-tau_k)
  conjugate(hat(phi_a)(tau'-tau_k))
 =L hat(v)(tau-tau'),

v=sum_a |phi_a|^2=psi^2.                              (MW4)
```

The right side is exactly the scalar-window kernel generated by `psi`. Analytic continuation gives the corresponding complex evaluation kernel wherever the transforms are defined.

Thus the theorem is not an accident of a chosen operator `B`: the two systems have the same physical frame operator.

## 5. Finite height-window consequence

The Zeta23 matrix uses only `0<=k<d`, not the full lattice. The exact coefficient coisometry need not preserve that finite Fourier interval. Nevertheless, for a fixed number of channels with uniform support and derivative bounds:

1. completion of the `k`-sum to `Z` produces `(MW4)`;
2. the omitted end terms are controlled by the same taper decay used in the paper;
3. the prime-side trace and Frobenius main terms depend only on `v=sum |phi_a|^2`;
4. the zero-side atom trace normalization depends only on the same complex-diagonal kernel.

Therefore the asymptotic first-two-moment certificate of every fixed coherent same-lattice multi-window family is the certificate of the single aggregate-power profile `v`, up to the same vanishing end errors.

At support at most one, optimizing that scalar profile is already the Montgomery–Taylor problem. Hence coherent same-lattice cross-window matrices do not improve the `0.67250...` scalar theorem.

## 6. Strength relative to the direct-sum theorem

The earlier direct-sum theorem covered only matrices of the form

```text
G_1 direct_sum ... direct_sum G_q.
```

Here the physical form may have every mixed channel entry

```text
B(f_(a,k),f_(b,l)), a not equal b,
```

and the coefficient matrix may be fully dense. The collapse still holds because all channels use the complete same modulation lattice.

## 7. Exact remaining window front

This theorem does **not** cover:

- channel-dependent sublattices or periodic omission of modulation indices;
- genuinely irregular center sets;
- a number of channels growing with the height parameter without uniform end control;
- additional arithmetic moments not determined by the compression spectrum;
- support beyond one.

The smallest genuinely new periodic window problem is therefore a polyphase system in which different windows occupy different residue classes of a coarser modulation lattice. After fiberization this becomes a matrix-valued symbol rather than the scalar aggregate power above.

## 8. Research consequence

Within the complete critical lattice,

```text
many tapers
+ arbitrary coherent channel mixing
+ all spectral moments of the resulting compression
=
one aggregate scalar power profile
+ redundant zero directions.
```

Thus a successful multi-window continuation must break same-lattice completeness, introduce new arithmetic support, or couple to the complete-kernel hierarchy through information not already present in the finite compression spectrum.
